draft.title: Roman religion
card: Romans were polytheists, which means they worshipped many gods. Jupiter was the king of the gods, Mars was the god of war and Venus was the goddess of love.
priests led festivals and made offerings at temples on behalf of the city. Romans believed that keeping the gods happy kept Rome safe.
each household made offerings to its own gods at a small shrine. The father usually led these prayers.

Christianity began in the eastern part of the empire and spread along Roman roads and sea routes. At first Christians were often punished. In the 300s CE it became the official religion of the empire.
draft.remember: Romans worshipped many gods in temples and at home. Christianity spread through the empire and became its official religion in the 300s CE.

a.q: Why are the Romans called polytheists?
opts: They did not worship any gods
a.why: Polytheist means a person who worships many gods, and Romans honoured gods such as Jupiter, Mars and Venus. Worshipping one god is monotheism, which is the opposite idea.
a.clue: Think about what poly means: many.

b.q: Livia lives in Rome in the 200s CE. Each morning her family leaves a small offering at a shrine in their house. What does this show?
opts: Romans also worshipped their gods at home
Romans only worshipped their gods at home
b.why: Households made offerings at their own shrines, so worship happened at home as well as in public. It was not the only place, because priests also led worship at temples.
b.clue: Look at where the offering is left.

b.best: Romans also worshipped their gods at home
